extracted.intended_audience: PR professionals, communications teams, and marketers who write and distribute press releases
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance for designing and distributing press releases optimized for shareability across journalists and social media audiences, covering visuals, structure, distribution, multimedia, measurement, and repurposing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Brand consistency
rubrics_metrics.description: Your press release needs to look like it belongs to your brand the moment someone sees it.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Apply logos, color palette, typography, and photography style across every asset so the release feels like a natural extension of your website and social presence; shared releases act as endorsements so ensure they reflect the brand professionally.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scroll-stopping visual design
rubrics_metrics.description: Create visuals that stop the scroll — product photos, infographics, and simple charts give readers’ eyes somewhere to land.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use one strong hero image at the top, supporting visuals that illustrate specific points in the body, and ample white space; avoid too many graphics (clutter) or too few (walls of text).

rubrics_metrics.name: Mobile optimization for visuals and load time
rubrics_metrics.description: Mobile optimization is non-negotiable: images must be appropriately sized to reduce load times, and alternative text must be included for accessibility.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: A release that takes ten seconds to load on mobile will never get shared; ensure images load quickly, are properly sized, and include alt text.

rubrics_metrics.name: Visual hierarchy and clean layout
rubrics_metrics.description: Clean layouts with clear visual hierarchy guide readers through your story and make sharing feel natural.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use visual hierarchy to lead the eye; balance information density with white space; strategic placement of visuals and headings improves readability and shareability.

rubrics_metrics.name: Inverted pyramid / lead with the news
rubrics_metrics.description: Use the inverted pyramid structure — put the most newsworthy information first.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Headline and first paragraph should contain everything someone needs to understand and share your story; opening paragraph must answer who, what, when, where, and why it matters so a reader scanning for 30 seconds gets the complete story.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scannability: subheadings, bullets, and short paragraphs
rubrics_metrics.description: Journalists and social users scan before they read; subheadings and bullet points are shareability tools.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use subheadings and bullet points as natural breaking points; keep paragraphs short (two to three sentences max), which works better on mobile and reduces intimidation for readers.

rubrics_metrics.name: Embed share mechanics (share bar and analytics)
rubrics_metrics.description: Include the actual mechanics of sharing built directly into the document, such as a 'Share This' bar.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Share bars provide analytics on what content generates the most interest and make distribution frictionless; use these tools to measure platform engagement and headline/image performance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Trackable links throughout the release
rubrics_metrics.description: Embed trackable links throughout your release, not just at the end.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Link products to product pages, studies to sources, and executives to bios/LinkedIn; links provide context and create multiple pathways for engagement and tracking.

rubrics_metrics.name: Hashtag and @mention strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Use one or two relevant, established hashtags and tag relevant accounts sparingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research which hashtags journalists and influencers follow; restraint is key—overuse (five or six hashtags) looks desperate; @mentions should be relevant and not turn the release into a free-for-all.

rubrics_metrics.name: "For more information" completeness
rubrics_metrics.description: The 'For more information' section should include direct links to relevant pages, media kits, high-resolution images, and contact information.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Make it absurdly easy for journalists to find what they need without sending follow-up emails; every additional required step reduces likelihood of coverage.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multimedia adds value, not decoration
rubrics_metrics.description: Multimedia elements — video, infographics, audio clips — increase shareability when used correctly; they should serve a specific purpose.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Only include multimedia that explains a concept, provides proof, or adds emotional resonance; if you can’t articulate why it improves shareability, cut it.

rubrics_metrics.name: Video best practices
rubrics_metrics.description: Videos work best when short (under 90 seconds), captioned for sound-off viewing, and provide information text can’t convey.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid autoplay that can't be paused; use video for demos, tours, or executive statements; ensure quick load times and captions for accessibility and social sharing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Infographic and audio use
rubrics_metrics.description: Infographics should distill complex data; audio clips work for interviews or sound bites that add personality.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Infographics must make sense at a glance; avoid requiring downloads for access; audio should add unique value and be easy to play.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose-driven visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Every visual element should serve a specific purpose: explain, prove, or add emotional resonance.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Treat visuals as substantive evidence/support, not decorative; cut visuals that don’t have a clear purpose.

rubrics_metrics.name: Targeted, personalized distribution
rubrics_metrics.description: Personalized outreach to small, carefully researched groups of journalists and influencers produces better pickup rates than generic mass blasts.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Segment distribution lists and customize pitch context for each segment (e.g., technology reporter vs. business reporter); the release can remain the same but tailor pitch emails and subject lines.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing and send-time strategy
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing matters—avoid sending at 2 a.m. or during major news events which guarantees burial.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Research when target journalists publish in your category; Tuesday–Thursday mornings generally perform better than Monday or Friday; work backward from publication timing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Appropriate use of distribution platforms
rubrics_metrics.description: Use distribution tools (Cision, PR Newswire, BuzzStream) for bulk sending and tracking when managing many releases; smaller campaigns may do better with direct email and social outreach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Paid platforms offer automation and tracking useful at scale; for targeted campaigns, direct outreach often yields better results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid overly promotional language
rubrics_metrics.description: Press releases that read like advertisements get ignored by journalists and mocked on social media.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Present newsworthy information rather than marketing copy; keep promotional language out of the release itself and reserve it for other channels.

rubrics_metrics.name: Avoid dense, jargon-heavy writing
rubrics_metrics.description: Dense paragraphs and jargon make press releases unreadable and unshareable.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Write for clarity first; if the release requires specialized knowledge to understand, you've lost most of your potential audience — prioritize plain language.

rubrics_metrics.name: Invest in high-quality visuals
rubrics_metrics.description: Missing or low-quality visuals signal you don’t take your news seriously.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use decent photography or high-quality, relevant stock images; poor visuals reduce shareability and perceived credibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Measure shareability with analytics and iterate
rubrics_metrics.description: Shareability is measurable: track which elements drive shares and adjust future releases accordingly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Use share-button analytics, link tracking, and social listening to see which headlines, images, and formats perform best; test, iterate, and build a library of what works for your organization.

rubrics_metrics.name: Repurpose content across channels
rubrics_metrics.description: Repurpose the release for blog posts, social updates, newsletters, and internal comms to maximize reach.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Pull quotes for Twitter, turn stats into Instagram graphics, extract key announcements for LinkedIn; treat the release as the centerpiece of integrated campaigns rather than a standalone document.
